apps.name: Pixel Guess
apps.subtitle: Guess the character behind the pixels
apps.description: An engaging web game where players identify pixelated images from categories like League of Legends, Valorant, and Demon Slayer.
apps.longDescription: Pixel Guess is a guessing game where you reveal hidden characters pixel by pixel. Pick a category, choose Easy or Hard difficulty, and try to identify the character before the image is fully revealed. Track your streak, compete on global leaderboards, and challenge yourself across multiple categories. Supports 12 languages.
features: Multiple categories: LoL, Valorant, Demon Slayer and more
Easy and Hard difficulty levels
Streak tracking and global leaderboards
Progressive pixel reveal mechanic
Available in 12 languages

apps.name: Pixel Guess Mobile
apps.subtitle: Pixel guessing game for iOS
apps.description: The mobile version of Pixel Guess — guess pixelated characters on your phone with smooth animations and native performance.
apps.longDescription: Pixel Guess Mobile brings the pixel guessing experience to your phone. Built with Expo and React Native, it features smooth Skia-powered animations, multiple game categories, Easy and Hard difficulty modes, streak tracking, global leaderboards, and confetti celebrations on correct guesses. Search characters with smart autocomplete and compete with players worldwide.
features: Native iOS app built with Expo
Skia-powered smooth animations
Multiple game categories
Easy and Hard difficulty modes
Streak tracking and global leaderboards
Smart autocomplete character search

apps.name: Hono Telescope
apps.subtitle: Monitoring dashboard for Hono apps
apps.description: An open-source monitoring and debugging tool for Hono applications. Real-time dashboard to inspect requests, exceptions, logs, and database queries.
apps.longDescription: Hono Telescope provides a real-time dashboard for Hono applications running on Node.js and Bun. Middleware-based setup gives you instant visibility into API requests with URL, method, response time, and status codes. Tracks unhandled exceptions with stack traces, collects console logs tied to request context, and monitors database queries from Prisma, Sequelize, MongoDB, and Bun SQLite with execution times.
features: Real-time request monitoring with response times
Exception tracking with stack traces
Log viewer tied to request context
Database query logging for Prisma, Sequelize, MongoDB
Simple middleware-based integration
MIT licensed and open source

apps.name: FontMapper
apps.subtitle: Map any website's fonts to your local fonts
apps.description: A Chrome extension that replaces any website's fonts with your favorite local fonts — per domain, instantly. Remembers your choices forever.
apps.longDescription: FontMapper lets each site you visit have its own typography that you personally control. Open the popup on any page, see every font the site is using, swap each one for any font installed on your machine, and FontMapper remembers your choices per domain — different rules for different sites, applied automatically on every visit. Uses Chrome's Local Font Access API for guaranteed PostScript-name matching, native CSS @font-face substitution for fast layout-preserving swaps, and zero data collection.
apps.requirements: Chrome 103+ (or any Chromium-based browser: Edge, Brave, Arc)
features: Per-domain font mapping — different rules for different sites
Searchable font picker with previews in each typeface
Hover to identify — highlights every element using a font
Instant preview, no page reload
Zero data collection, all stored locally

apps.name: tailwind-hitslop
apps.subtitle: Hit-slop touch targets for Tailwind CSS
apps.description: A Tailwind CSS plugin that invisibly expands an element's touch area while its visual size stays exactly the same — the web equivalent of React Native's hitSlop.
apps.longDescription: tailwind-hitslop adds hit-slop utilities to Tailwind CSS, expanding the interactive area of small targets — 16px icons, dense toolbars, close buttons — without changing their visual size or touching layout. It works on both Tailwind v4 (a pure-CSS @import built on the @utility and --value() primitives) and v3 (a classic config plugin), resolved automatically from one package with identical utilities on either version. Directional and axis utilities stack freely, an ::after family covers elements whose ::before is already taken, and a debug mode visualizes the expanded areas. Pure CSS, zero JavaScript, zero config — and compile-tested against the real Tailwind compiler.
features: Expands touch targets without changing visual size or layout
One package for both Tailwind v4 (CSS @import) and v3 (config plugin)
Pure CSS, zero JavaScript, zero config
Directional and axis utilities that stack freely
::after family for elements whose ::before is taken, plus a debug mode
Compile-tested against the real Tailwind compiler
